```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(ocrinfer)
```

## One pair of strings

```{r}
cer("In principio", "In principlo")
wer("erat verbum", "erat uerbum")

align_text(
  "In principio",
  "In principlo",
  unit = "grapheme"
)
```

## Why Unicode normalization matters

The visible character é can be represented in more than one Unicode form.
By default, `ocrinfer` applies NFC before evaluation.

```{r}
composed <- "\u00e9"
decomposed <- "e\u0301"

cer(composed, decomposed, unicode = "none")
cer(composed, decomposed, unicode = "NFC")
```

## A table of predictions

```{r}
predictions <- data.frame(
  line_id = c("l1", "l2"),
  system = c("A", "A"),
  reference = c("In principio", "erat verbum"),
  hypothesis = c("In principlo", "erat uerbum")
)

evaluate_recognition(
  predictions,
  truth = reference,
  prediction = hypothesis,
  id = line_id,
  system = system
)
```
